statements.status_notes: PostgreSQL fixed CVE-2026-120151 (PostgreSQL plpgsql record-field type confusion executes arbitrary code) in 16.16 on the PostgreSQL 16 branch: https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-120151/ lists 16.16 as the fixed release for major version 16, and the 16.16 release notes, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/16.16/, list this CVE. The fix is commit https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/cac94a04012879057070b1793a8110368be914bd on the REL_16_STABLE branch, which changes src/pl/plpgsql/src/pl_exec.c so that plpgsql re-checks a RECORD variable's field type and column number after casting the assigned value, in case the cast changed the record's row type; it is tagged Security: CVE-2026-120151 and is in the REL_16_16 release tag and not in REL_16_15. PL/pgSQL is built into the postgresql16 package as /usr/lib/postgresql16/plpgsql.so. The DHI postgresql16 packages for Alpine 3.23 are built from Alpine's postgresql16 APKBUILD, https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/859fa0795e895af033fab32094a83301f2b4d8ff/community/postgresql16/APKBUILD, which builds the upstream PostgreSQL release tarball; none of the patches it applies touch the files this fix changes. We checked the postgres server binary, /usr/libexec/postgresql16/postgres, in every postgresql16 build published for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI package repository as of 2026-11-28, on both x86_64 and aarch64 (package checksums verified against the package index): 16.16-r0 reports PostgreSQL 16.16 and carries the fix, while the earlier builds 16.13-r0, 16.14-r0 and 16.15-r0 report 16.13, 16.14 and 16.15 and are affected. As a check, the PL/pgSQL module, /usr/lib/postgresql16/plpgsql.so, in the postgresql16 package contains the error message this fix adds, which ends 'changed type during assignment', in 16.16-r0 on both architectures, and the same file in 16.13-r0, 16.14-r0 and 16.15-r0 does not. 16.16-r0 is the first published build that carries the fix. Alpine's postgresql16 APKBUILD lists CVE-2026-120151 under its 16.16-r0 secfixes.

PostgreSQL fixed CVE-2026-120151 (PostgreSQL plpgsql record-field type confusion executes arbitrary code) in 17.12 on the PostgreSQL 17 branch: https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-120151/ lists 17.12 as the fixed release for major version 17, and the 17.12 release notes, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/17.12/, list this CVE. The fix is commit https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/3a3eb761619cfd24fb3817628ccec699f2cc9187 on the REL_17_STABLE branch, which changes src/pl/plpgsql/src/pl_exec.c so that assigning to a record field rechecks the field's type and column number after casting the value when the record's row type changed; it is tagged Security: CVE-2026-120151, and it is in the REL_17_12 release tag and not in REL_17_11. PL/pgSQL, /usr/lib/postgresql17/plpgsql.so, ships in the postgresql17 package. The DHI postgresql17 packages for Alpine 3.23 are built from Alpine's postgresql17 APKBUILD, currently https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/ce22298320177ae25085d86fbf3b4fc1150c16a2/main/postgresql17/APKBUILD, which builds the upstream PostgreSQL release tarball; none of the patches it applies touch the source files this fix changes. We checked the postgres server binary, /usr/libexec/postgresql17/postgres, in every published postgresql17 package for Alpine 3.23 on both x86_64 and aarch64 (checksums verified against the package index): 17.12-r0 reports PostgreSQL 17.12 and carries the fix, while the earlier builds 17.7-r0, 17.8-r0, 17.9-r0, 17.10-r0 and 17.11-r0 report 17.7, 17.8, 17.9, 17.10 and 17.11 and are affected. As a check, plpgsql.so in the postgresql17 package contains the error message this fix adds ('record "%s" field "%s" changed type during assignment') in 17.12-r0 on both architectures, and the same file in 17.7-r0, 17.8-r0, 17.9-r0, 17.10-r0 and 17.11-r0 does not; the existing message 'record "%s" has no field "%s"' is present in every build. 17.12-r0 is the first published build that carries the fix. Alpine's postgresql17 APKBUILD lists CVE-2026-120151 under its 17.12-r0 secfixes.

PostgreSQL fixed CVE-2026-120151 (PostgreSQL plpgsql record-field type confusion executes arbitrary code) in 18.7 for major version 18: https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-120151/ lists 18.7 as the fixed release for 18, and the 18.7 release notes, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/18.7/, list this CVE. The fix is commit https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/6b1ca1333b346926515e62ae361781028b222f7d on the REL_18_STABLE branch, tagged Security: CVE-2026-120151 and Backpatch-through: 14, in the REL_18_7 release tag and not in REL_18_6. It changes only src/pl/plpgsql/src/pl_exec.c, so that exec_assign_value() rechecks a record field's type and column number after casting the value if the record's tuple type changed. The DHI postgresql18 packages for Alpine 3.23 are built from Alpine's postgresql18 APKBUILD, https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/59a1f1d230675807d5a95a0c1e57ba5d640ba039/main/postgresql18/APKBUILD, which builds the upstream PostgreSQL release tarball; none of the patches it applies touch the files this fix changes, and it lists CVE-2026-120151 under its 18.7-r0 secfixes. The DHI Alpine 3.23 package repository (x86_64 and aarch64) publishes packages built from source postgresql18 at 18.1-r0, 18.2-r0, 18.3-r0, 18.4-r0, 18.6-r0 and 18.7-r0. The vulnerable code is in the PL/pgSQL language handler, /usr/lib/postgresql18/plpgsql.so, which the postgresql18 package ships in every one of those builds on both architectures. We checked every published postgresql18 package for Alpine 3.23 on both x86_64 and aarch64 (checksums verified against the package index): the postgres server binary in 18.7-r0 reports PostgreSQL 18.7, while the earlier builds 18.1-r0, 18.2-r0, 18.3-r0, 18.4-r0 and 18.6-r0 report 18.1, 18.2, 18.3, 18.4 and 18.6. As a check, the error message the fix adds to plpgsql.so, record "%s" field "%s" changed type during assignment, appears in the 18.7-r0 postgresql18 package on both architectures and in no earlier build, while the existing message record "%s" has no field "%s" appears in every build. The earlier builds are upstream releases before 18.7, so they are affected; 18.7-r0 is the first published build that carries the fix.

PostgreSQL fixed CVE-2026-120151, type confusion in PL/pgSQL record-field assignment that lets an object creator execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database, in 17.12. Within major version 17, releases before 17.12 are affected. https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-120151/, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/17.12/. Debian fixed it for trixie in postgresql-17 17.12-0+deb13u1 (DSA-6625-1): https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-120151. The postgres server binary in this owner's 17.12-0 build and in its rebuild of Debian's 17.12-0+deb13u1 reports PostgreSQL 17.12 on amd64 and arm64, so both carry the fix, and 17.12-0 is the lowest published build that does. The 17.11-1 build and the current rebuild of Debian's 17.11-0+deb13u1 report PostgreSQL 17.11, and the earlier rebuilds of Debian's 17.10-0+deb13u1 and 17.11-0+deb13u1, no longer in the repository, package PostgreSQL 17.10 and 17.11. All of these are affected and sort below 17.12-0.
